TB3.status: FIRED (provisional on materiality; owner to confirm)
TB3.evidence: Rule: 'New export restrictions enacted that materially cut Nvidia's addressable market'. Enacted: BIS interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors', filed 2026-11-16, effective 2026-11-19. New restriction: licences for advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, and for any data center worldwide giving large compute to China-HQ (D:5) companies; existing providers have 90 days (~2027-02-17). It meets the trigger this committee pre-committed to on 2026-11-15 (worldwide or SE-Asia rule covering existing cloud/remote-access channels, licensing not notification); re-defining it now would be moving the goalposts. Materiality is unquantified: the Q4 guide already assumes zero China DC compute, China Hopper was $2.4B last quarter, FY26 China-HQ revenue $19.7B, a licence is not a denial, the Diffusion Rule was rescinded, and 'Singapore-billed sales near half of revenue' (FT) is billing location, not end use. Un-fire test: licence grants for the large SG/MY operators or a company quantification showing small at-risk revenue before ~2027-02-17, judged by the owner on evidence, not price.
